new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand classification: main stress on the word-initial syllable with secondary stresses on alternate syllables thereafter, but the primary description (Kofod 1978) is flagged as noting many exceptions to the initial-stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Category I implies rhythmic secondary stress on alternate syllables after the initial main stress; Goedemans does not indicate whether final syllables may bear secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Code (E): 'the descriptive source notes many exceptions to the general rule' - nature of the exceptions (lexical, morphological, weight) not stated by Goedemans; only Kofod 1978:28-31 would say.
new_statements.domain_note: Typological survey entry at word level; no data, no statement about citation forms vs connected speech. Primary statement (Kofod 1978, reportedly pp.28-31, intonation p.32) not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same language (Miriwung = Miriwoong, glottocode miri1266, ISO mep; Tindale T310 in Goedemans). Kofod 1978 is based on fieldwork at Kununurra from 1971; no dialect split is at issue.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both listed works were marked silent, and both were re-read in full (not just spot-checked): neither says anything about Miriwoong stress, accent, tone or phonology. Nothing missed. Prelims also checked: contents page only, no phonology. Not a listed work, but for the record: the prelims contents show Olawsky 2010 'Revitalisation strategies for Miriwoong' (ch. 12, p. 146) as the volume's only Miriwoong-specific chapter, as the reader noted.
